newsitem.title: USA: Pixar to shift interactive staff to movies.
newsitem.headline: Pixar to shift interactive staff to movies.

text.p: Pixar Animation Studios Monday said that, has a result of its partnership with Walt Disney Co, the company is redirecting all of the 62 personnel in its interactive division to work on its second feature film, "BUGS", its made for home video Toy Story Sequel and other film related projects.
Pixar's interactive division created two CD-ROMs, the Toy Story Animated Storybook and the Toy Story Activity Center, both released in 1996 through Disney Interactive.

Although Pixar's CD-ROMs have sold a combined total of almost one million units to date, the overall market for CD- ROM based interactive entertainment has not matured as many had hoped and predicted.

"The uncertain future of this market, combined with Pixar's enhanced opportunities to create longer format film and made for home video products under its new partnership with Disney, triggered Pixar's decision to redirect its valuable talent," the company said.

"While we enjoyed creating two very successful CD-ROM titles, we are now focusing our talent where our greatest opportunities lie and that's with movies under our new partnership with Disney," said Steve Jobs, chairman and chief executive of Pixar. "We don't mind putting all our eggs in just one basket now that we own half of the basket."
